outcomeNote: a mishna stating rulings and one reason clause; no argument and no named parties.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין לֹא לְתוֹךְ יַמִּים, וְלֹא לְתוֹךְ נְהָרוֹת, וְלֹא לְתוֹךְ כֵּלִים, אֲבָל שׁוֹחֵט הוּא לְתוֹךְ עוּגָה שֶׁל מַיִם. וּבִסְפִינָה, עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים. אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין לַגּוּמָּא כׇּל עִיקָּר, אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה גּוּמָּא בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס הַדָּם לְתוֹכָהּ. וּבַשּׁוּק לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה כֵּן, שֶׁלֹּא
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may not slaughter» an animal and have its blood flow, «neither into seas, nor into rivers, nor into vessels,» as in all those cases it appears that he is slaughtering the animal in the manner of idolaters. «But one may slaughter» an animal and have its blood flow «into a round excavation» containing «water. And on a ship,» one may slaughter an animal «onto vessels» as it is clear that his objective is to avoid sullying the ship. «One may not slaughter» an animal and have its blood flow «into a small hole» in the ground «at all, but one may fashion a small hole inside his house so that the blood will enter into it. And in the marketplace one may not do so,» so «that» he will «not»

moves.summary: the mishna rules where blood of slaughter may and may not be allowed to flow
gives the reason for the marketplace prohibition: not to emulate the heretics
